prerequisites: Solid knowledge of engineering mathematics, in particular: complex numbers, differential equations.
Basic knowledge of measurement and electrical engineering, in particular: complex AC technology, frequency response.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know the classical methods for designing single-input single-output control loops.
They master the basics of the Laplace transform and can use it for designing control loops.

Transfer functions for describing linear systems (differential equations with constant coefficients) are used by them as a matter of course for simple systems with and without compensation as an aid for controller programming.
Students apply mathematical methods to describe technical systems and can gain deeper insights into dynamic behavior based on simulation results.
From this, they derive conclusions for the design of appropriate automation concepts.

syllabus_topics: Concepts of control engineering (graphical modeling, feedback)
Properties and characteristics of the closed control loop (quality criteria, stability)
Control loops with PID controllers (Graphical design of P-controllers, tuning rules for P(I)(D)-controllers, compensation controllers/pole-placement)
Bode diagram (construction, stability according to Nyquist, controller design with lead and lag elements)
assessment_rules: Graded assessment is a written exam as per the valid study regulations. Ungraded assessment is experimental work consisting of approximately 5 experiments. Both must be successfully completed to be awarded ECTS credits.
